To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RPE is a major site of protein degradation and that defects in the proteolytic pathways of the RPE contribute to the pathology associated with AMD.
the RPE is the major degradatory pathway for the neural retina, and that failure of proteostasis is an underlying mechanism in the pathophysiology of age-related macular degeneration.
defects in the proteasome, autophagy and lysosomes in the retinal epithelial cell are associated with age related changes in the retina and the development of age related macular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the proteostatic balance between protein synthesis, folding and degradation in the RPE.
the mechanisms that underlie age related accumulation of lipofuscins in the RPE.
elucidation of the role of the ubiquitin proteasome, autophagy, and phagocytotic pathways in AMD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proteostasis in the RPE is impaired in AMD, but the precise mechanism(s) and the relative importance of each proteolytic pathway remain to be determined.
the RPE is a dynamic and highly active cell that has a critical role in maintaining protein homeostasis and that the failure to do so contributes to the pathogenesis of AMD.
proteostasis in RPE is compromised in AMD and that proteostasis is a potential target for the treatment of AMD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RPE is a highly active proteolytic tissue and the failure in its ability to degrade its cargo leads to the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates.
the proteasomal and lysosomal systems in the RPE become dysfunctional with aging and that this dysfunction is exacerbated by oxidative damage and inflammatory cytokine production in the RPE.
the accumulation of damaged proteins and lipofuscin in RPE is a consequence of defects in the proteostatic machinery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RPE is an excellent model for studying protein degradation and its involvement in the pathology of AMD.
the proteasome, heat shock proteins, phagocytotic and autophagic pathways, and lysosomal enzymatic activities are all involved in the pathobiology associated with AMD.
a failure in the RPE to maintain homeostasis by regulating protein turnover may be a key event in the initiation of AMD.
